title: Dark mode
description: Add a dark theme and a way to switch to it, independent of the app's language setting (LODGY-30). Requested directly by wardens using the app at night/in dim common areas. Depends on LODGY-36 landing first - dark mode should adjust the same RAG status-color tokens LODGY-36 defines, not invent its own.
acceptanceCriteria: A dark color scheme exists for LodgyTheme with adequate contrast on all screens
Warden can switch between Light/Dark/System default from the More tab
Switching applies immediately without restarting the app

history.note: Added from the v2 feedback session (warden interviews after the v1 field test) and from buried enhancement/limitation notes surfaced while re-reading the full v1 board history.
Added an explicit dependency on LODGY-36 (RAG color tokens) - sequence that ticket first so this one adjusts the same tokens instead of the two drifting independently.

Starting - LODGY-36's tokens are in, so this is a ThemePreferences DataStore (Light/Dark/System), a ThemeViewModel feeding LodgyTheme in MainActivity, and a picker in More. Reading the preference as a Flow so the switch recomposes in place; no activity recreate, unlike the language switcher which has to go through AppCompatDelegate.

Dark mode landed on top of LODGY-36's tokens. data/prefs/ThemePreferences.kt stores LIGHT/DARK/SYSTEM in its own DataStore (unknown/absent value reads as SYSTEM); ui/theme/ThemeViewModel.kt exposes it as a StateFlow and writes changes back. MainActivity collects it and resolves SYSTEM through isSystemInDarkTheme() before handing darkTheme to LodgyTheme, which already picks DarkStatusColors for the same flag - so dark mode adjusts LODGY-36's RAG tokens rather than defining any of its own. The picker is More -> Appearance; it applies on tap with no confirm and no activity recreate (unlike the language switcher, which has to go through AppCompatDelegate), because both the dialog and MainActivity read the same DataStore flow. Darkened LodgySecondary/LodgyError into DarkColors so the dark scheme is not carrying light-scheme accents. Renamed LanguageOptionRow to OptionRow now that both dialogs use it. ThemeViewModelTest covers stored value, the SYSTEM fallback, and persistence. testDebugUnitTest green.

FAIL on AC1 - the PIN lock screen is broken in dark mode, and it is the first screen the warden sees on every single launch. AC2, AC3 and AC4 all pass: More > Appearance offers Light/Dark/System default, selecting Dark recoloured the app instantly with no restart, and the choice survived a force-stop. But AC1 says 'adequate contrast on all screens' and PinLockScreen is not. WHAT I DID: set Appearance to Dark, force-stopped the app, relaunched. WHAT I EXPECTED: the lock screen in dark, like every other screen. WHAT HAPPENED: a broken mixed state - a light/near-white page background with dark-grey keypad buttons and near-black digits drawn on them. The digits 1-0 are barely readable and 'Enter your PIN' is pale grey on white. It does not settle after loading; it stays that way until you unlock. ROOT CAUSE (found in code): LodgyTheme (ui/theme/Theme.kt) calls MaterialTheme(...) directly and never wraps content in a Surface. Nothing therefore paints a themed window background - the light background is coming from the static android:windowBackground in the XML theme - and LocalContentColor is never set to onSurface, so text falls back to near-black. Every other screen hides this because it uses a Scaffold, which supplies both its own background and its content colour. PinLockScreen has no Scaffold (grep: 0 occurrences; PinSetupScreen has 2, which is why first-run setup looked fine). SUGGESTED FIX: wrap the content of LodgyTheme in a Surface(color = colorScheme.background) so the theme paints its own ground and sets content colour, rather than bolting a Scaffold onto this one screen. Please re-check the PIN setup screen in dark once fixed - it renders correctly today only because it happens to use a Scaffold.

Fixed in the theme, as QA suggested, rather than by bolting a Scaffold onto the one screen. LodgyTheme now wraps its content in `Surface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(), color = colorScheme.background)`, so the theme paints its own ground and sets LocalContentColor from the scheme. Previously MaterialTheme(...) was called with content passed straight through, so nothing painted a background - the window fell back to the static android:windowBackground (light) while components resolved their own dark colours, producing the light-page/dark-keypad/near-black-digit mix. Every other screen masked this by using a Scaffold. VERIFIED ON EMULATOR: with Appearance still set to Dark from QA's session, force-stopped and relaunched - the PIN lock screen now renders a dark background with light, fully legible digits and a readable 'Enter your PIN'. Re-checked the rest of the app in dark (invoice list, tenant profile, printable records) and nothing regressed; Scaffold screens simply overdraw the same background colour. Build and full suite green: 412 tests pass (4 new), ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest and assembleDebug both successful. Tests touched for the new signatures: TenantProfileViewModelTest and TenantDirectoryViewModelTest now mock the observed agreement flows, InvoiceListViewModelTest gains the ReconciliationRepository mock, and DataPacketTest gains the noticeGiven label. Note on two profile tests: they assert state after setPlannedMoveOut, which previously passed only because the ViewModel wrote the value optimistically. Rather than keep that second source of truth - the exact bug class LODGY-33 is about - the mocks now use a MutableStateFlow that re-emits on write, which is how Room actually behaves.
